goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 passes feed-controlled HTML through raw_html, bypassing sanitization and enabling stored XSS

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code flow: In poll_feed.rb:31, content is passed to TopicEmbed.import(). In topic_embed.rb:20, PostCreator is called with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. In post.rb:131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook() method returns raw content directly without any processing. The content from RSS feeds (i.content.content) is only passed through CGI.unescapeHTML and .scrub, which don't sanitize HTML for XSS. The raw HTML is then stored and rendered directly. This is a legitimate stored XSS vulnerability where malicious RSS feed content could inject scripts that execute when users view the embedded posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 validates only the initial hostname and follows redirects without revalidation, allowing SSRF through an open redirect on an allowed host

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, lib/topic_retriever.rb validates the host at line 15 with `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`. The code then calls `fetch_http` which uses `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`. In app/models/topic_embed.rb, `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` using ruby's open-uri. The finding claims that redirects are followed without revalidation, allowing SSRF through an open redirect. However, examining the code: (1) The initial URL host is validated against embeddable_host, (2) open-uri does follow redirects by default, (3) If an attacker controls an open redirect on the allowed host, they could redirect to internal resources. This is a valid SSRF concern - the code validates the initial URL but open-uri will follow redirects to arbitrary destinations. This is a real security issue where an open redirect on the embeddable_host could be exploited to access internal resources.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 adds a non-null column with a default, rewriting and exclusively locking the posts table and potentially causing production downtime

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb which adds a non-null column with a default value to the posts table. In older versions of PostgreSQL (before 11), adding a NOT NULL column with a DEFAULT requires rewriting the entire table and holding an exclusive lock, which can cause significant downtime on large tables. Looking at the migration: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. This is a legitimate concern for production databases with large posts tables. However, this depends on the PostgreSQL version being used - PostgreSQL 11+ handles this without table rewrites. The codebase appears to be from 2013 (based on migration dates), when PostgreSQL 11 wasn't available yet, making this a valid concern. This is a real operational/performance issue that could cause production downtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:18 uses an unprotected check-then-create sequence, allowing concurrent workers to create duplicate topics, race on the unique embed_url index, and abort a non-retrying feed poll

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb, the import method does: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `if embed.blank?` then creates a topic and TopicEmbed. This is a classic check-then-act race condition. Two concurrent workers could both see embed.blank? as true and both attempt to create topics. The database has a unique index on embed_url (from the migration), so one would fail with a unique constraint violation. In poll_feed.rb, the job iterates over RSS items calling TopicEmbed.import for each, and in topic_retriever.rb's perform_retrieve, it also calls import. The job has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, meaning if the unique constraint violation raises an exception, the job won't retry. This is a real race condition that could cause duplicate topic creation attempts and job failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7 reloads failed or impossible retrievals forever and enqueues a new job on every reload, causing permanent queue churn

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, app/views/embed/loading.html.erb sets a 30-second reload timer. The embed_controller.rb#best action shows that when no topic_id is found, it enqueues a Jobs::RetrieveTopic job and renders 'loading'. On each page reload, the controller will check TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) again - if it returns nil, it enqueues another job. The TopicRetriever has throttling (retrieved_recently? checks redis with 60-second expiry), but the page reloads every 30 seconds. So after the first 60 seconds, subsequent reloads could enqueue new jobs. However, the more significant issue is that if the retrieval permanently fails (invalid URL, unreachable site, etc.), the page will reload forever with no escape condition. This is a real issue - the loading page has no mechanism to stop reloading if retrieval is impossible, and while there's some throttling, repeated reloads will still cause queue churn over time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 compares and indexes unnormalized URL strings, allowing equivalent URL variants to create duplicate topics and bypass per-URL throttling

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, TopicEmbed.import uses `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` to check for existing embeds, and TopicRetriever uses `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`. The URLs are stored and compared as-is without normalization. This means URLs like 'http://example.com/page' and 'http://example.com/page/' or 'http://example.com/page?a=1&b=2' and 'http://example.com/page?b=2&a=1' would be treated as different URLs, potentially creating duplicate topics for the same content. The database migration also creates a unique index on embed_url without normalization. This is a real correctness issue - equivalent URLs could bypass the duplicate detection and create multiple topics for the same embedded content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 limits embed_url to 255 characters, so valid longer HTTP URLs pass request validation but fail during record insertion

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration file db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb, the embed_url column is defined as `t.string :embed_url, null: false`. In Rails, a string column without an explicit limit defaults to 255 characters in most databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL). The finding claims this could cause issues with longer URLs. However, examining the diff, I don't see any explicit limit being set - the column is just `t.string :embed_url`. While it's true that string columns typically default to 255 chars, this is a database-level constraint that would exist regardless. The code does accept URLs via params and stores them, but there's no explicit validation or truncation. URLs longer than 255 characters are relatively rare but possible. This is a real potential issue where a valid long URL could pass application-level validation but fail at database insertion time, causing an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 only absolutizes root-relative paths, leaving ordinary relative links to resolve against the wrong host or path

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 52-70, the code checks if href.start_with?('/') for links and src.start_with?('/') for images. This means it only handles root-relative URLs (like '/hello' or '/images/wat.jpg'). However, ordinary relative URLs without a leading slash (like 'hello.html' or 'images/wat.jpg') would not be processed and would remain as relative URLs. When these are rendered in Discourse, they would resolve against Discourse's domain rather than the original source domain, leading to broken links. The test in the spec confirms this behavior - it only tests root-relative paths. This is a real correctness issue where relative URLs (non-root-relative) are not properly absolutized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:34 ignores title changes for existing embeds, preventing title-only feed updates and title corrections

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the import method in topic_embed.rb, when an embed already exists (lines 30-37), the code only checks if content_sha1 has changed and updates the post content accordingly. The title is never updated for existing embeds - only the content is revised via PostRevisor. This is a real functional limitation where if a feed item's title changes but content stays the same, or if only the title needs correction, the update won't be applied. The code explicitly handles content updates but has no logic for title updates on existing embeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:140 loses the imported thread's created_at when using TopicEmbed.import_remote, giving original posts current timestamps while replies retain historical timestamps and corrupting chronology

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the old code in disqus.thor used PostCreator.new with created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) to preserve the original thread's creation timestamp. The new code replaces this with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]), which does not pass the created_at parameter. Looking at TopicEmbed.import_remote and TopicEmbed.import methods, neither accepts nor passes a created_at parameter to PostCreator. This means the original thread's timestamp is lost and the post will be created with the current timestamp, while child posts (replies) in the loop still use their original timestamps. This is a real bug that corrupts chronological ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114 removes the --category/-c option without replacement, breaking CLI compatibility and forcing imported Disqus topics into the default category

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the --category/-c option is indeed removed (lines 117 and 144-147 show the removal of the method_option and the code that used it). The import method now uses TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator.new with a category parameter. This is a breaking change for users who relied on the --category flag to specify where imported Disqus topics should be placed. The finding correctly identifies that this CLI option is removed without replacement, which would break existing scripts or workflows that use this option.
